sectionProgressions.description: Bouncy, syncopated jazz-minor cadence outlining complex 9th and altered dominant harmonies over a trap-bossa beat
Deceptive resolution to Bbmaj7 before plunging through A7alt into the blistering D Phrygian cascade
Aggressive low-end groove contrasting the open D pedal against the flamenco Neapolitan half-step Eb chord
Expansive harmonic finale utilizing sharp-11 and flat-9 chord extensions to push harmonic complexity to its peak

harmonicFunction: Dm9 (i9) - Minor tonic with warm major 9th extension (E) providing a sophisticated neo-classical foundation
Gm9 (iv9) - Minor subdominant opening the melodic field with lush upper chord extensions
A7b9#5 (V7b9#5) - Altered dominant chord borrowed from D Harmonic Minor / Phrygian Dominant, creating sharp resolution urgency
Bbmaj7 (VImaj7) - Deceptive resolution chord providing an uplifting harmonic contrast before plunging back to D minor
Eb/D (bII/i) - Neapolitan half-step neighbor chord over the low D pedal establishing signature flamenco grit

techniques.name: Selective Picking
techniques.description: Modern technical innovation combining economy picking with left-hand hammer-ons from nowhere to execute rapid phrases without picking every note

notes: Minimizes pick motion by substituting pick strikes with left-hand hammer-ons directly onto the fretboard
Enables lightning-fast phrases on acoustic/nylon strings with zero pick drag
Requires extreme left-hand finger strength and immaculate muting of idle strings
Produces a fluid, bubbly articulation that sounds somewhere between picking and legato
Pioneered by Tim Henson and Scott LePage to define modern math-rock and prog guitar
sequence: Pick the first note of a multi-string phrase firmly with a downstroke
Hammer-on the next note using only left-hand percussive force—do not pick
Cross to the adjacent string with an upstroke or middle-finger pluck
Immediately mute the previously played string with the fretting hand index pad
Repeat in rhythmic synchronization with the backing sixteenth-note grid
tips: Keep the pick close to the strings—any excess pick displacement wastes precious milliseconds
Use the fleshy side of the fretting index finger to mute higher unplayed strings
Keep amp gain low to clean up accidental string touches and unwanted harmonics
Practice the intro motif at 50% tempo until every hammer-on matches the volume of picked notes
Use a small, stiff jazz pick (like a Dunlop Flow 1.5mm or Jazz III) for maximum tip control
details.progression: Selective picking runs over Dm9 - Gm9

techniques.name: Nylon-String Thumping
techniques.description: Adapting modern slap-bass mechanics (Victor Wooten / Tosin Abasi thumb slapping and index popping) to nylon-string guitar

notes: Thumb strikes through the low D string like a slap bass hammer, using the knuckle joint
Index or middle finger immediately follows with an upward pop on the G or B string
Produces a tight, acoustic kick-and-snare percussive loop within the guitar arrangement
Nylon strings require precise velocity to avoid flabby buzz against the frets
Allows a single guitar to emulate both the 808 trap kick drum and hi-hat rolls
sequence: Position the right-hand thumb parallel to the low D string over the 15th-17th fret zone
Rotate the forearm sharply from the elbow/wrist to strike the string with the bony edge of the thumb
Immediately hook index finger beneath the 3rd or 4th string and snap upward
Combine with left-hand fretting slaps (dead-note slaps) for percussive syncopation
Loop the basic thump-pop pattern at 75 BPM before increasing speed
tips: Do not swing from the whole arm—keep the kinetic energy centered in the wrist rotation
Strike through the string rather than bouncing off it for maximum low-frequency fundamental
Set compressor attack fast enough to catch aggressive transient pops without volume spikes
Keep the fingernail away from the thumb strike zone to avoid chipping or breaking nails
Practice without backing track to ensure the percussive pulse is perfectly in time

techniques.name: Natural Harmonics & Flamenco Rasgueado
techniques.description: Rapid multi-finger strumming sweeps combined with chimey bell-like natural harmonics at the 12th, 7th, and 5th frets

notes: Lightly touching the string nodes at frets 12, 7, and 5 produces pure sine-wave overtone chimes
Harmonics are woven seamlessly into fast single-note runs for dynamic contrast
Flamenco rasgueado rolls flick individual fingers (pinky, ring, middle, index) in rapid succession
Creates the unmistakable Spanish guitar theatricality in the bridge and outro sections
Requires razor-sharp timing to prevent deadened notes
sequence: Locate harmonic sweet spots directly above the fret wire (not between the frets)
Touch string lightly with finger pad, pick firmly, and lift finger immediately upon release
Practice chaining 12th fret, 7th fret, and 5th fret harmonics across strings 1, 2, and 3
Incorporate the four-finger rasgueado flick across the full Dm9 chord
Transition instantly back into single-note selective picking without hesitation
tips: Touch the string with minimal pressure—pressing too hard converts the harmonic into a fretted note
Pluck near the bridge to maximize harmonic brilliance and sustain
Ensure your fingernails are buffed for a smooth rasgueado fan across strings
Use subtle stereo reverb to allow the harmonic overtone ring to trail gracefully
Keep left-hand positioning precise—even 2 millimeters off the fret wire dims the harmonic

sections.name: Intro - Bossa / Flamenco Theme
sections.description: The viral opening hook blending bossa nova groove with rapid Spanish Phrygian selective picking runs on nylon string
notes: Drop D tuning gives the Dm9 chord an immense, warm low end
Sixteenth-note runs use selective picking: pick first note, hammer-on the rest
Hybrid picking middle finger plucks high E string while pick strikes inner strings
Staccato muting with the fretting palm gives the notes a bouncy, articulate character

sections.name: Spanish Phrygian Triplet Cascade
sections.description: Blistering three-notes-per-string descending cascade tracing D Phrygian Dominant at high speed
notes: Demands seamless synchronization between left-hand pull-offs and right-hand string tracking
Outlines the flat-second (Eb) and major-third (F#) intervals of D Phrygian Dominant
Keep right-hand pick motion strictly economical
Ends with a snappy low D pedal thump that punctuates the trap drop

sections.name: Thump Groove & Slap Breakdown
sections.description: Heavy trap-influenced percussive breakdown with thumb slaps on the low D and finger pops on high strings
notes: Thumb slaps the 6th string to simulate an 808 kick drum pulse
Index pops the 3rd and 2nd strings like a crisp hi-hat / snare articulation
Neapolitan Eb/D chord creates menacing flamenco dissonance over the low D drone
Accented dead-note left-hand mutes create syncopated rhythmic polyrhythms

sections.name: Melodic Outro Climax
sections.description: The triumphant grand finale combining soaring melodic leads, natural harmonic flourishes, and aggressive flamenco strums
notes: Lyrical high-register theme soaring above dense trap percussion
Natural harmonic accents at frets 12 and 7 create twinkling overtone sparkle
Full-chord rasgueado bursts punctuate the cadence transitions
Final Dm9 chord sustained with shimmering ambient reverb and tape delay decay

beginner.title: Familiarize with D Phrygian Dominant & Selective Picking
steps: Tune 6th string down one step to D (Drop D tuning)
Memorize the D Phrygian Dominant scale shape in 5th and 7th fret positions
Practice selective picking: pick the first note, hammer-on the next two from nowhere
Mute unplayed strings with the fretting hand index pad to eliminate string buzz
Practice shifting cleanly between Dm9 and A7b9 chord grips at 60 BPM
beginner.goals: Execute clean single-string selective picking articulation at 75 BPM

intermediate.title: Coordinate Hybrid Picking and Thumping Grooves
steps: Integrate right-hand middle finger plucks with flatpick downstrokes
Practice thumb slapping on the 6th string followed by index pop on the 3rd string
Work through the main bossa theme at 80 BPM maintaining steady sixteenth-note swing
Master the natural harmonic chime nodes at frets 12, 7, and 5 with light touch
Eliminate unwanted sympathetic string vibration during staccato breaks
intermediate.goals: Play the main theme and slap breakdown cleanly at 100 BPM

advanced.title: Full-Speed Virtuosity & Triplets at 135 BPM
steps: Build the Phrygian triplet cascade up to the full 135 BPM tempo
Achieve dynamic balance between thumb slaps, finger pops, and picked notes
Execute seamless switches between nylon-string slapping, picking, and sweeping
Maintain razor-sharp staccato muting without slowing down or missing beats
Perform the entire song cleanly against the original backing track at 135 BPM
advanced.goals: Performance-ready execution of Playing God at full 135 BPM with relaxed precision

commonMistakes: Relying strictly on alternate picking instead of selective picking and hammer-ons from nowhere
Playing through an overdriven guitar amp which creates muddiness and masks the nylon-string attack
Failing to mute idle strings, causing harsh polytonal dissonance during rapid position shifts
Slapping the 6th string with excessive arm force, creating fret rattle instead of tight punch
Rushing sixteenth-note Phrygian cascades ahead of the metronomic trap beat
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: D Phrygian Dominant scale three-notes-per-string warm-up at 80 BPM
15 minutes: Selective picking isolation on the intro motif with crystal clean tone
15 minutes: Thumping and slap-pop mechanics drills across strings 6, 4, and 3
10 minutes: Triplet cascade metronome work increasing by 3 BPM increments
10 minutes: Full song playthrough recording and analyzing timing against the click
focusAreas: Selective picking efficiency and minimal pick motion
Left-hand hammer-ons from nowhere with equalized note volume
Nylon-string thumb slap and pop dynamic control
D Phrygian Dominant harmonic visualization across the fretboard
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 70 BPM with sixteenth-note subdivision clicks
Drill the intro phrase for 5 consecutive clean repetitions before raising tempo
Increase by 3-5 BPM steps, targeting 105 BPM as the primary fluency checkpoint
Practice at 140 BPM in short 2-measure bursts to build speed overhead
Settle at 135 BPM and lock into the relaxed, bouncy trap/bossa groove
